description: Pure mathematics, mechanics and statistics for CAIE 9709.
name: Mathematics

topics.title: Quadratics
topics.summary: Revise completing the square, discriminant and roots, quadratic equations/inequalities.

topics.title: Functions
topics.summary: Revise domain/range, composite and inverse functions, graph transformations.

topics.title: Coordinate geometry
topics.summary: Find equations of lines and circles, and use gradients, midpoints and distances to solve geometric problems.

topics.title: Circular measure
topics.summary: Work in radians rather than degrees to find arc lengths and sector areas — and to keep calculus with trig functions valid later on.

topics.title: Trigonometry
topics.summary: Revise graphs, identities, equations.

topics.title: Series
topics.summary: Recognise and sum arithmetic and geometric sequences, including sums to infinity, and expand (1+x)ⁿ using the binomial theorem.

topics.title: Differentiation
topics.summary: Revise derivatives, tangents/normals, stationary points and optimisation.

topics.title: Integration
topics.summary: Revise indefinite/definite integration, areas, volumes of revolution.

topics.title: Algebra
topics.summary: Handle modulus functions, divide and factorise polynomials, and split algebraic fractions into partial fractions.

topics.title: Logarithmic and exponential functions
topics.summary: Use the laws of logarithms and exponentials to solve equations and model exponential growth or decay.

topics.title: Trigonometry
topics.summary: Extend trig identities and equation-solving, and work with inverse trig functions (arcsin, arccos, arctan).

topics.title: Differentiation
topics.summary: Apply the product, quotient and chain rules to differentiate more complex combinations of functions.

topics.title: Integration
topics.summary: Integrate using substitution and standard forms, and use integration to find areas under more complex curves.

topics.title: Numerical solution of equations
topics.summary: Locate roots of equations you can't solve algebraically using iteration, and justify how accurate your answer is.

topics.title: Algebra
topics.summary: Extend algebraic technique to harder polynomials, partial fractions with repeated or quadratic factors, and the general binomial expansion for any rational n.

topics.title: Logarithmic and exponential functions
topics.summary: Use natural logarithms and e to solve equations and model real-world growth/decay contexts.

topics.title: Trigonometry
topics.summary: Use compound and double-angle identities and the R sin(x+α) form to solve harder trig equations and find max/min values.

topics.title: Differentiation
topics.summary: Differentiate implicitly and parametrically, on top of product/quotient/chain rules, for curves not given simply as y = f(x).

topics.title: Integration
topics.summary: Use integration by parts, substitution and partial fractions to integrate a wider range of functions, including trig integrals.

topics.title: Numerical solution of equations
topics.summary: Apply iterative methods to harder equations, justifying convergence and the accuracy of your final answer.

topics.title: Vectors
topics.summary: Revise 3D lines, dot product, angles/intersections.

topics.title: Differential equations
topics.summary: Form and solve first-order differential equations by separating variables, using given initial conditions to find a particular solution.

topics.title: Complex numbers
topics.summary: Revise Argand diagrams, modulus/argument, polar form.

topics.title: Forces and equilibrium
topics.summary: Draw force diagrams, resolve forces into components, and apply equilibrium conditions including friction.

topics.title: Kinematics of motion in a straight line
topics.summary: Use SUVAT equations, motion graphs and calculus to describe motion in a straight line, including under gravity.

topics.title: Momentum
topics.summary: Apply conservation of momentum and impulse to collisions between particles.

topics.title: Newton's laws of motion
topics.summary: Apply F = ma to connected particles, pulleys and inclined planes.

topics.title: Energy, work and power
topics.summary: Calculate work done, kinetic/gravitational potential energy, and power in mechanical systems.

topics.title: Representation of data
topics.summary: Summarise and display data using histograms and cumulative frequency diagrams, and calculate mean, variance and standard deviation.

topics.title: Permutations and combinations
topics.summary: Count arrangements (order matters) and selections (order doesn't) using factorials, permutations and combinations.

topics.title: Probability
topics.summary: Use tree diagrams and Venn diagrams to handle conditional probability and test for independence.

topics.title: Discrete random variables
topics.summary: Build probability distributions, calculate expectation and variance, and apply the binomial distribution.

topics.title: The normal distribution
topics.summary: Standardise normal variables to find probabilities, and use the inverse normal to find an unknown value or parameter.

topics.title: The Poisson distribution
topics.summary: Model random events over a fixed time/space interval with the Poisson distribution, and know when it approximates the binomial.

topics.title: Linear combinations of random variables
topics.summary: Find the expectation and variance of sums and differences of independent random variables.

topics.title: Continuous random variables
topics.summary: Use probability density functions and integration to find probabilities, expectation and variance for continuous variables.

topics.title: Sampling and estimation
topics.summary: Understand sampling distributions and construct confidence intervals to estimate an unknown population parameter.

topics.title: Hypothesis tests
topics.summary: Set up null and alternative hypotheses, use a critical region or p-value, and draw a conclusion in the context of the question.

resources.title: Topical questions + worked solutions
resources.description: Current 9709 questions by topic for P1, P3, M1 and S1

description: Theory, problem-solving and programming for CAIE 9618.
name: Computer Science

topics.title: Data Representation
topics.summary: Convert between binary, denary and hexadecimal, use two's complement and BCD, and perform binary addition/shifts while spotting overflow.

topics.title: Multimedia
topics.summary: Understand how bitmap and vector images and sampled sound are represented digitally, and calculate resulting file sizes.

topics.title: Compression
topics.summary: Compare lossy and lossless compression and the trade-off each makes between file size and quality.

topics.title: Networks including the internet
topics.summary: Distinguish LANs from WANs, know the hardware/media involved, and understand IP addresses, MAC addresses, DNS and URLs.

topics.title: Computers and their components
topics.summary: Identify the core hardware components of a computer system, including embedded systems and memory/storage/input-output devices.

topics.title: Logic Gates and Logic Circuits
topics.summary: Revise truth tables, logic expressions, circuit design.

topics.title: Central Processing Unit (CPU) Architecture
topics.summary: Revise ALU/CU/registers, buses, fetch-decode-execute, interrupts/performance.

topics.title: Assembly Language
topics.summary: Read and trace simple assembly language programs, understanding opcodes, operands and addressing modes.

topics.title: Bit manipulation
topics.summary: Use logical shifts, masks and bitwise operators to manipulate individual bits within a byte.

topics.title: Operating Systems
topics.summary: Understand the OS's role in managing processes, memory, files, the user interface and security.

topics.title: Language Translators
topics.summary: Compare compilers, interpreters and assemblers, and understand the stages of translating source code.

topics.title: Data Security
topics.summary: Identify common security threats and the defences (authentication, access control, firewalls, backups) used against them.

topics.title: Data Integrity
topics.summary: Use validation and verification methods, plus parity checks and check digits, to catch data errors.

topics.title: Ethics and Ownership
topics.summary: Consider privacy, copyright/licensing and the wider ethical impact of computing on society.

topics.title: Database Concepts
topics.summary: Understand tables, records, fields, keys and relationships, and the basic idea behind normalisation.

topics.title: Database Management Systems (DBMS)
topics.summary: Understand the DBMS's role in managing the data dictionary, access rights, backup/recovery and concurrent access.

topics.title: DDL and DML
topics.summary: Revise definition/manipulation, SQL-style SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.

topics.title: Computational Thinking Skills
topics.summary: Apply decomposition, abstraction and pattern recognition to break down and design solutions to a problem.

topics.title: Algorithms
topics.summary: Revise pseudocode/flowcharts, searching/sorting, trace tables.

topics.title: Data Types and Records
topics.summary: Choose appropriate primitive data types and group related data together using records.

topics.title: Arrays
topics.summary: Declare, index and traverse one- and two-dimensional arrays.

topics.title: Files
topics.summary: Open, read from, write to and close files, processing records sequentially while checking for end-of-file.

topics.title: Introduction to Abstract Data Types (ADT)
topics.summary: Revise stacks, queues, linked-list concepts.

topics.title: Programming Basics
topics.summary: Use variables, constants, operators and input/output statements — the building blocks of any program.

topics.title: Constructs
topics.summary: Use selection (IF) and iteration (FOR/WHILE/REPEAT) constructs, including nested constructs, to control program flow.

topics.title: Structured Programming
topics.summary: Break programs into procedures and functions with parameters, improving modularity and controlling variable scope.

topics.title: Program Development Life Cycle
topics.summary: Follow the stages of analysis, design, coding, testing and maintenance when developing software.

topics.title: Program Design
topics.summary: Use structure charts and pseudocode to design a program's structure and data before coding it.

topics.title: Program Testing and Maintenance
topics.summary: Design normal, boundary and erroneous test data, and know the different types of maintenance (corrective, adaptive, perfective).

topics.title: User-defined data types
topics.summary: Define your own enumerated and composite data types where the built-in primitive types aren't specific enough.

topics.title: File organisation and access
topics.summary: Compare serial, sequential and direct (random) file access, and understand indexing and hashing for fast lookup.

topics.title: Floating-point numbers, representation and manipulation
topics.summary: Represent real numbers using a mantissa and exponent, understand normalisation, and the trade-off between precision and range.

topics.title: Protocols
topics.summary: Understand why network protocols exist and compare examples that handle addressing, transport and application-level communication.

topics.title: Circuit switching, packet switching
topics.summary: Compare how circuit switching and packet switching route data across a network, and the trade-offs of each.

topics.title: Processors, Parallel Processing and Virtual Machines
topics.summary: Understand multi-core processors, pipelining, and how virtual machines abstract away physical hardware.

topics.title: Boolean Algebra and Logic Circuits
topics.summary: Revise Boolean laws, De Morgan, simplification.

topics.title: Purposes of an Operating System (OS)
topics.summary: Understand how the OS schedules processes, manages memory and handles interrupts.

topics.title: Translation Software
topics.summary: Understand the stages of compilation in more depth, including the role of linkers, loaders and libraries.

topics.title: Encryption, Encryption Protocols and Digital Certificates
topics.summary: Compare symmetric and asymmetric encryption, and understand how digital signatures and certificates verify identity.

topics.title: Artificial Intelligence
topics.summary: Understand the basic ideas behind machine learning, expert systems and neural networks, and the ethical questions AI raises.

topics.title: Algorithms
topics.summary: Extend algorithm knowledge to more advanced examples, and compare efficiency using Big O.

topics.title: Recursion
topics.summary: Write and trace recursive algorithms, understanding base cases, recursive cases, and how the call stack behaves.

topics.title: Programming Paradigms
topics.summary: Revise procedural, OOP, declarative.

topics.title: File Processing and Exception Handling
topics.summary: Write robust file-processing code using exception handling to recover gracefully from errors.

description: Applied analysis, strategy and evaluation for CAIE 9609.
name: Business

topics.title: Enterprise
topics.summary: Understand business activity, added value and opportunity cost, and the role entrepreneurs and intrapreneurs play in taking risks.

topics.title: Business structure
topics.summary: Compare economic sectors and forms of business ownership, from sole traders to public limited companies and social enterprises.

topics.title: Size of business
topics.summary: Compare ways to measure business size, and the different advantages small and large firms have.

topics.title: Business objectives
topics.summary: Set business objectives, including SMART targets, and consider corporate social responsibility.

topics.title: Stakeholders in a business
topics.summary: Identify stakeholder groups, understand how their interests can conflict, and who a business is really accountable to.

topics.title: Human resource management
topics.summary: Plan workforce needs, and understand the recruitment, selection, training and redundancy process.

topics.title: Motivation
topics.summary: Revise motivation theories, financial methods, non-financial methods.

topics.title: Management
topics.summary: Understand the core functions of management and how they shape decision-making and manager effectiveness.

topics.title: The nature of marketing
topics.summary: Understand marketing objectives, market vs product orientation, and how demand and supply interact.

topics.title: Market research
topics.summary: Compare primary and secondary market research methods, sampling techniques, and issues of reliability and bias.

topics.title: The marketing mix
topics.summary: Revise product, price, promotion, place.

topics.title: The nature of operations
topics.summary: Revise transformation process, productivity, job/batch/flow production.

topics.title: Inventory management
topics.summary: Balance buffer inventory against reorder levels and lead times, including the just-in-time approach.

topics.title: Capacity utilisation and outsourcing
topics.summary: Calculate capacity utilisation, and weigh the costs/benefits of outsourcing against over- or under-capacity.

topics.title: Business finance
topics.summary: Understand why businesses need finance, the difference between cash and profit, and the idea of working capital.

topics.title: Sources of finance
topics.summary: Revise internal sources, external sources, matching finance to context.

topics.title: Forecasting and managing cash flows
topics.summary: Construct cash-flow forecasts, calculate net cash flow, and identify ways to manage a cash shortage.

topics.title: Costs
topics.summary: Classify costs as fixed or variable, calculate contribution, and use break-even analysis including margin of safety.

topics.title: Budgets
topics.summary: Understand the purpose of different budget types and how to interpret variances between budgeted and actual figures.

topics.title: External influences on business activity
topics.summary: Revise political/legal/economic/social/tech factors, international trade, sustainability.

topics.title: Business strategy
topics.summary: Revise SWOT/PEST, Porter five forces, Ansoff, decision trees/force-field/scenario planning.

topics.title: Organisational structure
topics.summary: Compare hierarchical, flat and matrix structures, and understand delegation, accountability and centralisation.

topics.title: Business communication
topics.summary: Compare communication methods and identify barriers that reduce how effective communication is.

topics.title: Leadership
topics.summary: Compare leadership styles and judge which suits a given business situation best.

topics.title: Human resource management strategy
topics.summary: Link HR strategy to employee performance and a business's ability to respond flexibly to change.

topics.title: Marketing analysis
topics.summary: Analyse market size, share and growth, use elasticity and forecasting, and assess customers and competitors.

topics.title: Marketing strategy
topics.summary: Apply segmentation, targeting and positioning, build an integrated marketing mix, and consider international marketing.

topics.title: Location and scale
topics.summary: Weigh up location factors for a business, and understand economies and diseconomies of scale.

topics.title: Quality management
topics.summary: Compare quality control, quality assurance and total quality management, and understand benchmarking.

topics.title: Operations strategy
topics.summary: Understand lean operations, the role of technology, and supply-chain decisions and trade-offs between capacity, cost and quality.

topics.title: Financial statements
topics.summary: Read an income statement, statement of financial position, and cash-flow statement.

topics.title: Analysis of published accounts
topics.summary: Calculate and interpret profitability and liquidity ratios, and understand their limits when comparing over time or between firms.

topics.title: Investment appraisal
topics.summary: Use payback period, average rate of return (ARR) and net present value (NPV) — alongside qualitative factors — to judge an investment.

topics.title: Finance and accounting strategy
topics.summary: Use financial data and annual reports strategically, tracking ratio trends and financial risk.

description: Physical, inorganic, organic and analytical chemistry for CAIE 9701.
name: Chemistry

topics.title: Atomic structure
topics.summary: Revise particles/isotopes, electron configuration, ionisation energy.

topics.title: Atoms, molecules and stoichiometry
topics.summary: Use moles to balance equations and calculate reacting masses, gas volumes and solution concentrations.

topics.title: Chemical bonding
topics.summary: Revise ionic/covalent/metallic, shape/polarity, intermolecular forces.

topics.title: States of matter
topics.summary: Use the particle model and the ideal gas equation, and understand the structures of solids.

topics.title: Chemical energetics
topics.summary: Revise enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond energies.

topics.title: Electrochemistry
topics.summary: Assign oxidation states, balance redox equations, and understand the process of electrolysis.

topics.title: Equilibria
topics.summary: Revise dynamic equilibrium, Kc, Le Chatelier.

topics.title: Reaction kinetics
topics.summary: Revise rate, collision theory, activation energy/catalysts.

topics.title: The Periodic Table: chemical periodicity
topics.summary: Explain trends across Period 3 in structure, bonding and the properties of oxides and chlorides.

topics.title: Group 2
topics.summary: Explain trends in reactivity, solubility and thermal stability down Group 2, and know some uses of Group 2 compounds.

topics.title: Group 17
topics.summary: Explain trends in oxidising power down Group 17, and use halide ion tests to identify halogens.

topics.title: Nitrogen and sulfur
topics.summary: Understand the chemistry of ammonia and nitrogen compounds, sulfur dioxide, and their environmental impact.

topics.title: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry
topics.summary: Revise nomenclature, isomerism, mechanisms.

topics.title: Hydrocarbons
topics.summary: Understand the reactions of alkanes (free-radical substitution) and alkenes (electrophilic addition).

topics.title: Halogen compounds
topics.summary: Understand nucleophilic substitution and elimination reactions of haloalkanes, and the factors affecting their reactivity.

topics.title: Hydroxy compounds
topics.summary: Understand the reactions of alcohols, including oxidation and dehydration.

topics.title: Carbonyl compounds
topics.summary: Distinguish aldehydes from ketones using chemical tests, and understand their addition/reduction reactions.

topics.title: Carboxylic acids and derivatives
topics.summary: Understand the reactions of carboxylic acids and the formation of esters and other derivatives.

topics.title: Nitrogen compounds
topics.summary: Understand the basicity of amines, and the structure of amino acids and the peptide link.

topics.title: Polymerisation
topics.summary: Distinguish addition and condensation polymerisation, and identify monomers from a given repeat unit.

topics.title: Organic synthesis
topics.summary: Plan multi-step synthetic routes between organic compounds, choosing the correct reagents and conditions.

topics.title: Analytical techniques
topics.summary: Interpret mass spectra and infrared spectra, and use chromatography to identify compounds.

topics.title: Chemical energetics
topics.summary: Use Born-Haber cycles and lattice energy, and consider entropy and Gibbs free energy to judge whether a reaction is feasible.

topics.title: Electrochemistry
topics.summary: Use standard electrode potentials to calculate cell potentials and predict whether a redox reaction is feasible.

topics.title: Equilibria
topics.summary: Work with Ka, Kw and pH for acids and bases, understand how buffers resist pH change, and use Ksp and partition coefficients.

topics.title: Reaction kinetics
topics.summary: Determine rate equations and orders of reaction from experimental data, and link mechanisms and catalysis to kinetics in more depth.

topics.title: Group 2
topics.summary: Extend Group 2 trends to explain thermal stability and solubility patterns in more quantitative detail.

topics.title: Chemistry of transition elements
topics.summary: Understand transition metal complexes and ligands, the origin of colour, and their role as catalysts.

topics.title: An introduction to A Level organic chemistry
topics.summary: Extend organic nomenclature to more complex molecules, understand aromatic (benzene) bonding, and optical isomerism.

topics.title: Hydrocarbons
topics.summary: Understand the structure of benzene and its characteristic electrophilic substitution reactions.

topics.title: Halogen compounds
topics.summary: Extend halogen compound chemistry to more complex mechanisms and reactivity patterns.

topics.title: Hydroxy compounds
topics.summary: Understand the chemistry of phenol alongside alcohols, and further synthetic routes between them.

topics.title: Carboxylic acids and derivatives
topics.summary: Understand the reactions of acyl chlorides and acyl substitution reactions in more depth.

topics.title: Nitrogen compounds
topics.summary: Understand phenylamine, azo dye formation, and the structure of amides and amino acids.

topics.title: Polymerisation
topics.summary: Understand condensation polymers in depth, predict monomers from a repeat unit, and consider polymer degradability.

topics.title: Organic synthesis
topics.summary: Build a complete organic reaction map, plan multi-step synthetic routes, and deduce structures from given information.

topics.title: Analytical techniques
topics.summary: Interpret chromatography, ¹H NMR and ¹³C NMR spectra, combining evidence from several techniques to identify structures.
